title: Hydrothermal Geochemical-Outflow Up-Dip Advection, Pluvial-Tufa-Decontaminated Sinter & Perched Clay-Cap Conduit Tensor (HGVC-20)
hypothesis: Blind geothermal faults missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS surface catalogue lose brittle scarp relief to smectite/argillic alteration while lateral groundwater flow shifts high-geothermometer outflow plumes (quartz, chalcedony, Na-K-Ca minus surface temperature) and shallow 1m-2m conductive thermal gradients 1-3 km down-bajada from the concealed feeder fault. Back-projecting cold-well-decontaminated geochemical disequilibrium and vertical probe gradients up the hydraulic and basement-depth dip onto perched smectite clay-cap conductivity residuals, hydrothermal magnetite-destruction troughs, tufa-decontaminated opaline sinter corridors, and cover-decoupled basement steps recovers concealed geothermal fault conduits across both relay zones and >2.5 km blind basins.
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan (~1330 m) and Lake Bonneville (~1555 m) shoreline carbonate tufa mounds (146/709 Paleo_geothermal_final.csv rows) and wave-cut benches, flat closed-basin playa evaporite brine collars (high raw cond_surf without basement step), and cold agricultural irrigation wells (Cold / temp_c < 18 C).
